tactics: Count the lines, words or list items before replying, and adjust until the count matches.
Reply with the requested text only: no title, no commentary, no quotation marks.
Keep every word the request forbids out of the answer.
When rewriting, change only what the instruction asks to change.
Prefer concrete nouns and strong verbs to adverbs.
When a length range is given, aim for the middle of it.

tasks.prompt: Write a poem about the sea that is exactly three lines long. Output the three lines and nothing else.
Write one sentence describing a forest that includes the words 'pine' and 'silence'.
Rewrite this sentence in the future tense and reply with the sentence only: He cooks dinner.
Correct the grammar and reply with the corrected sentence only: She don't likes apples.
Write a news headline of at most 6 words about a new library opening. Reply with the headline only.
Write a numbered list of exactly four steps for making a cup of tea. Output only the list.
Rewrite this in at least 15 words, keeping the meaning, and reply with the sentence only: The train was late.
Describe a winter morning in one sentence without using the words 'very' or 'cold'.
Split this into two sentences and reply with them only: The rain stopped and the children went outside.
Write a title on the first line and a one-sentence summary on the second line, about a lost cat. Output two lines only.
Replace the word 'walked' with a stronger synonym in this sentence and reply with the sentence only: She walked into the room.
Write a description of a wool blanket in 30 to 45 words.
